observations.statement: External precedent, endpoint-class split after a manifested phenotype: across 39 sources in two bounded searches (173 rows; no source in both), post-onset arms (adult arms included) by endpoint class, studies counted in each outcome column where they have a row: seizure or network 13 studies (9 full, 7 partial, 3 none); cognition and behaviour 13 (4 full, 8 partial, 6 none); neuronal structure 7 (4, 3, 2, one not measured); survival 6 (1 full, 4 partial, 2 worse, 1 not measured); motor 7 (2, 3, 3); myelin and glia 4 (2 full, 2 partial, all in glial or metabolic lesions, see O10); systemic and metabolic 4.
observations.comparison: treated against untreated same-genotype comparator, per source
observations.readout: seizure, network, behaviour, cognition, structure, survival, motor
observations.direction_observed: recovery varies by endpoint class and within single papers; failures sit inside otherwise positive papers
observations.limits: Not WWOX evidence. A tabulation of studies, not a meta-analysis; models differ in gene, lesion, lifespan and assay; negative cells are under-counted by publication selection. Built from age_at_restoration_vs_onset and outcome only (status_vocab is not used: the two producers read it differently). Endpoint classes are normalised across the two tables; behaviour and cognition cells were re-binned after review.

observations.statement: External precedent, spontaneous seizure endpoints after onset: complete rescue of spontaneous and provoked seizures in one conditional channel model treated after manifest seizures and again in adults with a within-animal two-week baseline, and partial recovery in one channel-transcript silencing model treated while symptomatic; no statistically significant reduction of epileptic spasms in a late arm of a kinase model (one conditional allele, heterozygous females, five late animals; the authors call seizure prevention limited after onset) or in a ligase model (conditional reactivation). In the same set an adult conditional restoration of a synaptic regulator eliminated interictal spiking measured in the same animals before and after.
observations.genotype: Scn1a haploinsufficiency; Kcnt1 gain of function; Cdkl5; Ube3a; Syngap1 (not WWOX)
observations.comparison: treated against control-virus or untreated same-genotype animals
observations.readout: video-EEG seizures, provoked threshold, interictal spiking
observations.direction_observed: recovered in two channel models, not in two non-channel conditional arms, recovered for interictal spiking in one non-channel regulator
observations.limits: Not WWOX evidence. Gene class correlates with the split and is not established as its cause: it is confounded with restoration mode, endpoint identity and the level of restoration achieved. The provoked-threshold result of the synaptic-regulator study holds at the tonic-clonic stage only. WWOX falls on the non-channel side. Spike-wave discharge rate is an interictal network measure, so its external precedent is split, not negative.

observations.statement: External precedent, the same ligase locus under a different restoration mode: antisense reactivation gave a full rescue of audiogenic seizure susceptibility at the same postnatal age at which conditional reactivation had left seizures in place, and rescued the electroencephalographic rhythm and sleep phenotype in juveniles and adults, with the degree of improvement correlated to the protein level reached; the same programme reports that cortical poly-spike frequency, its epileptiform endpoint, was not reduced at either age (PMID 36594817).
observations.readout: audiogenic susceptibility, EEG rhythm and sleep, poly-spike frequency
observations.direction_observed: rhythm and provoked threshold recovered; epileptiform poly-spike frequency not reduced
observations.limits: Not WWOX evidence. Read at full text for both sources by the R1 package; the restoration level reached was partial and regionally uneven, which the authors offer as a candidate explanation of the poly-spike result. One gene.

observations.statement: External precedent, myelin and white matter: in the gene families searched first no study restored or corrected the gene after a documented onset of a myelin phenotype and then measured myelin sheath structure; two hypomyelination models were treated before onset and the sheath moved least in both (about a tenth of control with reduced compaction in one, below control in the other) while apoptosis, glial markers and, in the antisense jimpy arm, oligodendrocyte number, respiration and lifespan moved far more, and a germline suppression of the toxic allele reached nearly half of the wild-type myelinated-axon count at three weeks (about 35 percent in the optic-nerve correlate), with incomplete compaction. Outside those families the class is not empty: an astrocyte-directed vector given seven months after the stated onset of white-matter vacuolation reversed vacuolation and water accumulation and a progressive motor deficit against a same-genotype comparator; a single systemic administration as late as P20 in a leukodystrophy null with a lifespan under one month globally improved myelination with residual lipid abnormalities (abstract); enzyme re-expression improved lineage markers with the effect blunted in old animals (abstract). One (an oligodendrocyte-enzyme lesion treated at six weeks while symptomatic; open full text read by an independent verifier, locator audit pending) reports electron-microscopic G-ratio, layers per axon and axon number as normalised; the others did not measure sheath morphometry; all correct a glial or metabolic lesion in the cell that carries it.
observations.comparison: treated against same-genotype comparator, per source
observations.readout: vacuolation, water content, myelin protein immunostaining, g-ratio where measured
observations.direction_observed: structural sheath endpoints moved least pre-onset; post-onset white-matter endpoints reversed in glial-gene lesions
observations.limits: Not WWOX evidence. The WWOX myelin deficit follows a neuronal defect and oligodendrocyte-lineage deletion is silent, so the cell to reach differs. Vacuolation and water content are not myelin. The structural readout in the lineage-restricted Mecp2 rows is myelin basic protein immunostaining thickness at postnatal day 16, not electron microscopy. Of the late sources, the oligodendrocyte-enzyme one has open full text and locates its arm (six weeks, symptomatic); the others are abstract level and one never locates onset. What is unmeasured: sheath morphometry after onset in a neuron-driven lesion. Bounded searches, not a statement that none exists.

observations.statement: External precedent, the age cliff and what it is evidence of: in a null of a DEE gene dying in the third postnatal week, a brain-directed vector supplying the missing protein extended lifespan, reduced seizure severity without changing time to first seizure and fully restored parvalbumin interneuron and pyramidal excitability when given at P2; at P10, at twice the exposure, all eight treated nulls died in the usual window. The authors attribute the later failure to transgene level and distribution, citing other work for reduced rodent CNS expression after the first postnatal days; the restoration achieved at the later age was never measured. The generalisation is route-, capsid- and promoter-specific: a single systemic administration at P20 rescued lethality in another short-lived null (abstract), and a systemic vector at four to five weeks produced a few percent neuronal transduction and a modest survival benefit (abstract).
observations.genotype: Scn1b null (DEE52); leukodystrophy null; short-lived null (not WWOX)
observations.age_stage: P2 versus P10; P20; four to five weeks
observations.comparison: treated against untreated and empty-vector same-genotype animals
observations.readout: survival, seizure severity, interneuron excitability, growth
observations.direction_observed: benefit at P2, none at P10 with restoration not measured; growth not rescued at either age
observations.limits: Not WWOX evidence. The P10 arm is UNVERIFIED, not a recovery failure. The two late-delivery sources are abstract level and one never locates onset. Growth failing even pre-onset makes growth and glycaemia primary rather than supportive endpoints in a WWOX arm.

observations.statement: External precedent, the cost of restoring and the need for a treated wild-type arm: abrupt widespread reactivation of the deficient gene killed animals selectively in the restored genotype in two independent models and both groups moved to graded induction; one intervention changed behaviour in treated wild-type animals (elevated plus maze, descriptive, read by its authors as benefit, so its direction is contested), and a second compound moved wild-type animals proportionally (to be checked against its row before the count is kept); without a treated wild-type arm an intervention effect is scored as a rescue. Modest vector-mediated overexpression in wild-type brain was tolerated in three sources, one of which also reports a separate deleterious effect of overexpression of its gene.
observations.direction_observed: hazard specific to abrupt conditional reactivation and to exposure, not to gene addition as such
observations.limits: Not WWOX evidence. No powered toxicity or tumour-surveillance endpoint; single exposures; hazards are gene-specific. WWOX overexpression has its own recorded signals (ectopic protein moved organoid readouts beyond wild type; applied recombinant protein lowered viability).

observations.statement: Human timing precedent, spinal muscular atrophy, single-administration vector replacement: treated before symptom onset, 14 of 14 infants sat independently for at least 30 seconds and 11 within the normal developmental window, and all were alive and free of permanent ventilation at 14 months, against none of 23 and 6 of 23 in a matched untreated natural-history cohort; 5 of 14 were below the normal gross-motor range at 18 months. The symptomatic comparison (64 and 44 percent reaching the same endpoint, months later) is a cross-trial secondary statement inside this report, flagged by its authors as limited by differing design, endpoints and eligibility; the symptomatic primary reports were not read.
observations.direction_observed: stage associated with outcome; stage not separated from eligibility
observations.limits: Never a WWOX expectation: a lower motor neuron disease with a peripheral endpoint, no seizure, interneuron or myelin endpoint, and a pre-symptomatic route that depends on newborn screening that does not exist here.

observations.statement: Human timing precedent, metachromatic leukodystrophy, ex-vivo lentiviral haematopoietic gene therapy: across the assessed treated cohort, which included early-symptomatic children, 20 of 25 showed normal acquisition of cognitive skills at ages at which the untreated cohort was severely impaired; treated groups exceeded a matched untreated cohort on gross motor function; the MRI white-matter and atrophy score stabilised in every treated group but plateaued at a worse level when treatment followed symptoms (the early-symptomatic course still differed significantly from the natural-history course); children entering the rapid progression phase did not benefit, two dying of progression despite documented engraftment in all treated patients.
observations.readout: gross motor function, cognitive acquisition, MRI score
observations.direction_observed: arrested at a stage-dependent plateau; no benefit in rapid progression
observations.limits: Never a WWOX expectation: benefit comes from cross-correction by engrafted donor-type myeloid progeny with a months-long latency, not restoration in the affected neural cell; no randomised comparator; a composite imaging severity score is not a myelin measurement.

inferred_add: That which endpoint classes could recover after onset is partly predictable from outside WWOX: circuit and physiology endpoints and some cellular structural endpoints have recovered after onset in several other single-gene models; developmentally built behaviours and tissue-level structure generally have not; spontaneous seizure endpoints are split by restoration mode, endpoint identity and level achieved rather than cleanly by gene class; white-matter abnormality has been reversed after a documented onset in glial or metabolic lesions, and the myelin sheath has not been measured after onset in a neuron-driven lesion in any of them. This is an expectation imported from other genes, not a WWOX result, and it changes no window_state.

That the perinatal efficacious window in the mouse is a biological boundary: the one comparable later-age experiment failed with the restoration achieved never measured, its authors attribute the failure to transgene level and distribution, and two other nulls with short lives were treated later with a modest survival benefit (abstract level); an observed perinatal-only window in a rodent is a candidate artefact of the modality until the restoration achieved at the later age is measured. This weakens 'WWOX restoration after onset cannot work' and equally forbids concluding that it can.
counter_evidence_add: A firing or interneuron-excitability endpoint used as a success criterion needs its acceptable direction fixed in advance: in the one external post-onset success with a cellular endpoint, fast-spiking excitability overshot wild type while the phenotype recovered (PMID 35013317).
Benefit decayed in one external model (four of 14 treated animals died between two and six months) and required re-treatment in another, so a short follow-up would miss both.

Human post-symptomatic treatment of a leukodystrophy failed outright in rapidly progressing cases with molecularly successful correction, and the structural white-matter endpoint was arrested at a stage-dependent plateau (O14).

Two external DEE models could not be asked the post-onset question at all, because death follows the first seizure; the absence of a post-onset arm in the WWOX literature is the field's normal condition for a lethal null.
do_not_assume_append: Do not read an external post-onset recovery as licence for a WWOX post-onset arm in the mouse: every external post-onset arm treats an animal that would otherwise reach adulthood, while the null in this corpus is dead at about three weeks; the constraint is as much vector kinetics (level and distribution achieved) as biology.
notes_append: External precedents (O7-O14) place post-onset recovery on record for seizure, network, cellular structural and some behavioural endpoints and for white-matter water and vacuolation in glial lesions; the myelin sheath structure after onset in a neuron-driven lesion, and interneuron number at any age, were not found in bounded searches.
